summary.text: In Indian agricultural economics (Directorate of Economics & Statistics, Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare / ICAR-IIPR), Gram (Cicer arietinum, Chickpea / Bengal Gram / Chana) is the undisputed king of Indian pulses, accounting for roughly 45% to 50% of the country's total pulse production and nearly 35% to 40% of its total pulse acreage. India is the world's largest producer and consumer of chickpeas, contributing over 70% of global output.

protection.name: Fusarium Wilt (Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. ciceris)
protection.geography: National Epidemic Hazard (Severe in MP, Maharashtra, Gujarat, UP)
protection.impact: Soil-borne systemic wilt; occurs in two waves: (1) Seedling stage (2–3 weeks after sowing): plants collapse and dry flat; (2) Reproductive stage: leaves turn dull grey-green, wilt, and dry up; internal vascular tissue shows dark brown to black discoloration when taproot is split longitudinally. Causes 15–60% field mortality.
protection.passage: Gram — source table 122, row 2. Management modes are descriptive; formulations, rates and schedules omitted.

protection.name: Gram Pod Borer (Helicoverpa armigera)
protection.geography: All Commercial Belts (The #1 Insect Pest across India)
protection.impact: Early larvae feed on tender foliage and floral buds; older larvae bore into green pods, keeping their head inside the pod while the rest of the body remains outside; hollows out developing seeds, leaving clean, circular entry holes; single larva can destroy 20–30 pods.
protection.passage: Gram — source table 122, row 3. Management modes are descriptive; formulations, rates and schedules omitted.

protection.name: Ascochyta Blight (Ascochyta rabiei)
protection.geography: Northern & Irrigated Belts (Heavy in Rajasthan, Haryana, Punjab)
protection.impact: Circular-to-oval brown spots on leaves, stems, and pods with concentric rings of dark pycnidia; lesions girdle stems, causing upper twigs to snap and die back; pods develop circular sunken lesions; can destroy 50–80% of crop during cool, cloudy, wet weather.
protection.passage: Gram — source table 122, row 4. Management modes are descriptive; formulations, rates and schedules omitted.

protection.name: Dry Root Rot (Rhizoctonia bataticola / Macrophomina phaseolina)
protection.impact: Post-flowering drought stress symptom; plants wilt and dry up suddenly in patches; lower stems show dark grey-black discoloration; taproot becomes brittle, devoid of lateral roots, and shreds like dry wood; bark sloughs off, revealing tiny black sclerotial bodies.
protection.passage: Gram — source table 122, row 5. Management modes are descriptive; formulations, rates and schedules omitted.

protection.name: Botrytis Grey Mold (BGM) (Botrytis cinerea)
protection.impact: Shedding of flowers and leaves; infected stems show dark, water-soaked lesions covered in a fuzzy grey mold; branches break off; pod formation is suppressed, or infected pods yield shriveled, discolored seeds.
protection.passage: Gram — source table 122, row 6. Management modes are descriptive; formulations, rates and schedules omitted.

protection.name: Pulse Beetle / Bruchid (Callosobruchus chinensis, C. maculatus)
protection.impact: Adult female lays small, white, oval eggs stuck to the seed surface; grubs burrow into the seed, feeding internally on the cotyledons; adults emerge leaving circular emergence holes; grain loses weight, germinability, and milling quality; turns lot into powdery frass.
protection.passage: Gram — source table 122, row 7. Management modes are descriptive; formulations, rates and schedules omitted.
